Do contraceptive methods change the vaginal environment?

Study B — 93 samples · pill / injectable / ring

Background & question

The setting

  • Hormonal contraception is used by millions of women, but its effect on the vaginal environment is not well mapped.
  • The “vaginal environment” has three layers we can measure: who is there (220 bacterial species), what the tissue is doing (~14,000 human genes), and immune signalling (15 cytokines).

Our two questions

  1. Do the three hormonal methods (pill, injectable, ring) produce different vaginal microbiomes or transcriptomes?
  2. Does community type — Lactobacillus-dominant vs diverse — explain gene activity better than the method does?

One-sentence take-home to open with: the methods barely differ; the community state is the stronger signal. The rest of the deck earns that sentence.

Study design

  • Cohort: 93 women, one sample each, cross-sectional.
  • Three arms: pill, injectable, ring — all hormonal, but the ring acts locally in the vagina while pill and injectable act systemically.
  • Three data types per sample: species counts (220 × 93), RNA-seq gene counts (14,226 × 93), cytokines (15 per sample).
  • Design is clean: sequencing batches are balanced across arms (47 vs 46 samples), and BV / STI prevalence is spread across arms — nothing is confounded with the method.
  • Key rule we follow: community type is defined from the species table only, then tested on the gene table — never define a group from one table and test that same table.

If asked why one sample per woman: this is a cross-sectional comparison between methods, not a before/after trial like the probiotic Study A.

Quality control — the gate before any test

Check Result
Count-table columns match metadata rows, both tables PASS
No duplicate or unmatched sample IDs PASS
All 220 species + all 14,226 genes annotated PASS
Metadata complete; bv label matches Nugent score bands PASS
Sequencing depth: shallowest sample 5,247 reads PASS — nothing near our 1,000-read line
Batch vs arm cross-table: no confounding PASS
Cytokines: B018, B029 missing all 15 values FLAG — dropped from cytokine analyses only

Sequencing depth of every sample, both tables (log scale). All samples sit well past the 1,000-read line.

Carry-forward: all 93 samples into microbiome & RNA-seq; 91 into cytokine analyses. Full audit trail with spot-checks: 01-qc-report.html.

Why the depth plot matters: a shallow sample behaves oddly in every downstream method. The shallowest microbiome sample has 5,247 reads — verify with min(colSums(d$species)) in 01-qc.qmd.

Why only “cytokine analyses only” for B018/B029: they are missing all 15 values (failed assay / lost tube), but their count tables are fine, so dropping them everywhere would waste two good sequencing samples.

Methods — and why we chose them

  • Community type: fraction of reads from Lactobacillus ≥ 50% → lacto-dominant (48 samples), else diverse (45). Both types occur in all three arms, so the two groupings are not copies of each other.
  • Overall differences: ordination (PCoA) + PERMANOVA (999 permutations, by = "margin").
    • Species: Bray–Curtis distance.
    • Genes: CLR transform + Euclidean — raw gene counts would let a few very highly expressed genes dominate Bray–Curtis.
  • Per-gene differences: DESeq2 on raw counts (never CPM or logged — it normalises itself), design ~ rnaseq_batch + arm (or + community), genes kept if ≥ 10 counts in ≥ 24 samples, FDR 0.05 across ~14,000 tests.
  • BV status included as a yardstick — a known biological effect, so our method effect has a sense of scale.

Choices to defend if asked:

  • Why batch in the design? QC showed it is balanced across arms, so it cannot fake a method effect — but only if it is in the model.
  • Why define community on species only? Testing a group on the table that defined it is circular; it guarantees a “significant” result.
  • Why FDR? ~14,000 genes tested at once — 5% of raw p-values would be false positives by chance alone (~700 genes!).

Results 1 — the methods barely differ

Test Result
Species PERMANOVA method R² ~3%, p ≈ 0.08 — vs ~22% for BV (yardstick)
Gene PERMANOVA method R² ~2.7%, not significant
DESeq2 pairwise (13,713 genes) injectable vs pill 10 FDR genes; ring vs pill and ring vs injectable ≈ 100–140 each

How to read this: the ordination plots show overlap, and the numbers agree — method never explains more than ~3% of variation. The one structure worth chasing is ring vs the two systemic methods; injectable and pill are nearly indistinguishable. And the yardstick matters: BV status explains ~22% of species composition, so a real biological effect in this data looks like 22%, not 3%.

Spot-check: results(dds_arm, contrast = c("arm", "injectable", "pill")), sum(padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE) should be 10.

Results 2 — community type leaves a gene signature

Community vs method, head-to-head on genes Result
Gene PERMANOVA (both terms in one model) method ~2.6% vs community ~1.5% — both ns
DESeq2 gene counts passing FDR community 310 vs best method contrast 136

The two lenses disagree, and that is the finding worth presenting:

  • The ordination (one pooled number) says neither grouping explains much.
  • The gene-by-gene test says community type finds > 2× more FDR-significant genes than the best method contrast (310 vs 136).

So community type is the stronger target if you want a gene list to interpret — the top genes are labelled in the volcano so you can eyeball whether they make biological sense. Spot-check: rerun sum(genes_by_community$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE) — it should be 310.

Choices we made

  • Community type defined from the species table only; tested on genes only. (Alternative not chosen: the circular test.)
  • A simple two-type split at 50% Lactobacillus, rather than a three-way L. crispatus / L. iners / Gardnerella split — we tried the three-way version and it explained no more of the gene ordination (R² 2.4% vs 1.5%) while being harder to explain.
  • Bray–Curtis for species, CLR + Euclidean for genes. (Alternative not chosen: Bray–Curtis on raw gene counts — dominated by library size.)
  • Batch included in every DESeq2 design; no samples dropped from the count tables. (Alternative not chosen: dropping B018/B029 everywhere.)
  • BV status as a yardstick, and by = "margin" PERMANOVA so each term gets credit only for what it adds.

Every choice here is documented with its rejected alternative in the two reports: 01-qc-report.html and 02-contraceptive-analysis.html.
